### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 87 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a51702529a726dc0994431daedbb2ab5aaffbfa` — the merge of head `97b94ed710055aa56eb2b6db2b1feaa02f381383` into base `b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a51702529a726dc0994431daedbb2ab5aaffbfa && git checkout 2a51702529a726dc0994431daedbb2ab5aaffbfa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923 97b94ed710055aa56eb2b6db2b1feaa02f381383 && git checkout -B drift-repro b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923 && git merge --no-ff 97b94ed710055aa56eb2b6db2b1feaa02f381383

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Epic red-line review — N #31670 · head 97b94ed7 · 2026-11-08T23:19Z

Verdict: **PASS on the epic's three red lines.** The lane seat (`domain:server#1`) keeps its own contract review, CI and landing. This record is the epic seat's part (ruling 6723571682).

Read: the diff against `main` (13 files, +1235): `namespace-co-owner-names.ts` in objectql and cli, `registry.ts` `installPackage`, `os validate` / `os build`, and the tests. Checked against ADR-0150 D2 (record 6724570466) and the plan's N row.

- **Red line 1, never loosens.** The diff only adds a refusal. No resolution path changes: phase 1's one-holder rule, `getItem` and R's resolver have no diff. The same package re-installing is skipped (`packageId` equality), so an upgrade is not refused against itself.
- **Red line 2, ambiguity named.** `NamespaceNameConflictError` carries every conflict and every existing holder. The message names them all. It reuses `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, an existing code, at 422.
- **Red line 3, releasable.** The narrowing is the one the N row declares (D2: a `(type, name)` held twice inside one namespace, for the 12 uncovered types), measured first-party 0 of 297. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right declaration. One predicate serves `installPackage`, `os validate` and `os build`, so the doors cannot disagree.

**The thread's three open questions, ruled:**
1. **Refuse at cold start, not warn: keep the refusal.** D2 as ruled says "refused at install and `os validate`", and boot installs each package. The first-party count is 0. A third-party deployment that holds such a pair learns at upgrade, loudly and with every holder named, which is the outcome red line 2 asks for. (This differs from E6's N2 on purpose: that was a *reference* the ADR declared refused at the read; this is an install door the ADR names.)
2. **`base`, `system` and `sys` not judged: accepted for this child.** It neither narrows nor loosens anything today. G1's qualified address must answer `409` with the candidates for a name two packages of one of these namespaces hold, and never pick, so red line 2 holds there. G1 #31691 carries that pin. The PR states the measured count of such duplicates on first-party trees. Child A (#31685) records the exemption in ADR-0150 D2.
3. **New public names** (`NAMESPACE_UNIQUE_TYPES`, `namespaceNameConflicts`, `NamespaceNameConflictError` and the rest of the objectql index exports): the seat's call, accepted as named. They follow R's export pattern.

Serial: K #31681 and G1 #31691 follow this one on `registry.ts` `installPackage`, on the same seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `97b94ed710055aa56eb2b6db2b1feaa02f381383`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-namespace-co-owner-names.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-namespace-name.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__namespace-co-owner-names.ts.json + packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-package-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-order.ts, packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/view-container-names.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (all read on `main`, never reviewed)

Inputs: card #31670 (body and both comments: the claim 6727391505 and the os-dev-report 6728539138), the epic's three red lines in the card body, ADR-0150 on `main` (D2, D9, execution plan row N), rulings 6723462584 / 6723499113 / 6723571682 / 6724570466, PR #31717 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...97b94ed7` (13 files, +1235/-0), and the check-runs on the head. Check-runs at the time of this record: every run that has concluded is `success` — Lint & Repo Gates and all eight Lint shards, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards; `Test Core (1/8 … 8/8)` and `Type Check · workspace` are still `in_progress`. Lint UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI are `skipped` (no `ui/` path in the diff). An `in_progress` run is not a pass: the seat lands only once those nine conclude `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the code it cites:

1. **The package door (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage`) refuses a package whose item of one of twelve types bears a name another installed package of the same `manifest.namespace` holds.** Right. `NAMESPACE_UNIQUE_TYPES` is exactly `sharing_rule, queue, assignment_rule, hook, job, app, page, dashboard, report, book, analytics_cube, tool` — ADR-0150's execution plan row N verbatim (`rag_pipeline` retired, as the row says) — and the vocabulary test pins the list and that it shares only `tool` with `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES`. No thirteenth type is reachable: `declaredNamespaceUniqueNames` iterates that frozen list only. Nothing beyond the declared twelve, so nothing goes to the maintainer.
2. **The declared-name readers match the engine's registration seams.** Right, checked against `engine-registration.ts` (`registerPackageBody`, `registerMetadataCollections`), `engine-package-registration.ts` (`registerPlugin`) and `engine-top-level.ts` (`METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`, `resolveMetadataItemName`, `registersManifestAsApp`): each collection is read by `singularToPlural(type)` and all twelve keys are own entries of the spec's map (`sharingRules`, `queues`, `assignmentRules`, `hooks`, `jobs`, `apps`, `pages`, `dashboards`, `reports`, `books`, `analyticsCubes`, `tools`); the item key is `name` else `id`, as `resolveMetadataItemName` reads it for every non-view key; the manifest-as-app row is `name && navigation && !apps?.length`, the engine's `registersManifestAsApp`; a nested `plugins[]` entry is read one level deep (the engine recurses no deeper), its `apps` skipped (not in `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`, and `registerPlugin` passes `apps: false`), and its plugin-as-app row is `plugin.name && plugin.navigation`, the engine's condition. A nested plugin's items are stamped under the parent id, so assigning its names to the parent's namespace is what the engine does.
3. **Not judged: a package with no namespace; `base`, `system`, `sys`; the environment catalog; the same package again; one package declaring a name twice; every other type.** Right. The shareable set equals `isShareableNamespace` on `main` (`RESERVED_NAMESPACES` + `sys`) and the test holds them equal; the sitting set is the installed package records only, so a `registerItem` with no package (the environment catalog, `sys_metadata` hydration) is never a holder; `other.packageId === incoming.packageId` is skipped, so a reload, re-install or upgrade of the same id passes (pinned), and `uninstallPackage` deletes the record, so an uninstall frees its names (pinned).
4. **No `collisionPolicy` downgrade.** Right — the same disposition as the security catalog, the default record page and the bare-name rules; pinned with `fresh('warn')`.
5. **Placement: after the ADR-0130 D3 object check, ahead of every mutation, at every install including the boot.** Right. The call sits between `refuseCoOwnedObjectNameCollision` and `refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts`, before `registerNamespace` and the record write; the test pins that a refused install leaves no record and no namespace ownership, and that an install refused by both D3 and this rule answers `DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_OBJECT_NAME`.
6. **`os validate` / `os build` refuse the artifact in the same sentence, exit 1, `errors` rows (`packageId`, `code`, `httpStatus`, `message`, `conflicts[]`), and `os build` writes no artifact.** Right. The CLI helper owns only the walk — `resolveArtifactPackageOrder(parsed)`, the boot's dependency-topological order — and calls `namespacePackageOf`, `namespaceNameConflicts` and `namespaceNameConflictMessage` from `@objectstack/objectql`; no second copy of the predicate or the sentence exists (the spawn test asserts the row message EQUAL to the door's thrown message). One undeclared side-effect rides along — see ② and ④ S1.
7. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/objectql` gains four values (`NAMESPACE_UNIQUE_TYPES`, `namespacePackageOf`, `namespaceNameConflicts`, `namespaceNameConflictMessage`) and three types (`NamespaceNameConflict`, `NamespacePackage`, `NamespaceUniqueType`); `NamespaceNameConflictError` stays unexported, as `BareNameConflictError`, `ArtifactObjectNameConflictError` and `NamespaceConflictError` are on `main`; no error code is minted (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE` was already exported). Right and consistent. `@objectstack/cli` gains an internal util only.
8. **Forced test rows.** The parity roster row belongs in `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` (both commands call it, cross-package by construction) — right. The injected-column ledger row keys the module-level site of the `queue` literal: the module spells `'queue'` twice, in the `NamespaceUniqueType` alias and the frozen list, both at module level, so one row under the module-level key is the correct count — right.
9. **ADR anchor.** Names ADR-0150 and ADR-0130; the module header spells both ids. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31670-namespace-co-owner-names.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `@objectstack/cli: minor`. Matches what the diff publishes: both packages move (objectql's door, exports and module; cli's two commands and util), no other package's source changes (`core`, `spec`, `metadata-protocol`, `runtime` are read, not edited). The `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING under AGENTS.md's level table and the title carries `!`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on a moved package — satisfied; `minor` is also what the four phase-1 bare-name changesets (#30836, #31006, #31093, #31375) took for the same class of refusal. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on the PR body and in the changeset with the same sentence; `Skills-docs: none — REASON` present; `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` present and correct (no stored shape changes, no key removed). Check Changeset is green. One wording gap: the Clause-② sentence names the two refusals of the twelve-type rule and says "Nothing is widened" — true — but does not name the two boot refusals the new walk lets through to `os validate` / `os build` (④ S1).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Cold boot refuses rather than warns (dev: keep refuse).** Agree — keep A. D2 is ruled as a refusal "at install and `os validate`, on the ADR-0130 D3 object check" (ADR-0150 row N; ruling 6724570466), and D3 refuses at every install, the boot included; phase 1's warn-at-boot posture belongs to an environment-wide backstop that ADR-0150 D9 retires per type, not to this rule. The population that would stop booting is measured 0 first-party and 0 of 297 on HotCRM (the card's reading; the dev marks HotCRM NOT MEASURED in this container, honestly). The changeset's "Who moves" names the upgrade consequence and the one-line fix. No escalation.
2. **`sys` / `base` / `system` not judged (dev: leave out).** Agree for this child — A. Mirrors `isShareableNamespace` and D3's co-owner map, measured 0 duplicates on showcase's 22 `sys` packages; cloud's `sys` packages NOT MEASURED, stated. ADR-0150 D2 does spell `sys/NAME` as an address, so the exemption is a bound on D2's guarantee, not a reading of it: the seat should carry it forward as a follow-up card (widen once cloud's `sys` packages are measured) rather than leave it in acceptance notes only. Not a blocker: the module, the anchor and the changeset all state the exemption.
3. **New public names.** Accept A. `NamespaceNameConflictError` follows the sibling classes' spelling and envelope; `NAMESPACE_UNIQUE_TYPES` / `namespacePackageOf` / `namespaceNameConflicts` / `namespaceNameConflictMessage` follow `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES` / `declaredBareNames` / `bareNameReason`. Two nits only (④ N4): the class differs from the existing `NamespaceConflictError` by one word, and the module file is `namespace-co-owner-names.ts` while its exports say `namespaceName*`. No new code — right: the condition is the one `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` registers for.
4. **Not raised by the dev, answered here:** the residual (④ N3), the hot re-registration order (④ N2), the record projection asymmetry (④ N1), and the core resolver's refusals surfacing at the CLI doors (④ S1).

### ④ Design judgment

Scenario accepted against: ADR-0150 D2 (one package holder per `(type, name)` inside a namespace, so `NAMESPACE/NAME` names one item), on ADR-0130 D3's object check in `installPackage`, under the epic's red lines.

**Red line 1 — resolution never loosens.** Holds. No reader is touched; `getItem`'s bare-slot-first answer and every first-registered fallback on `main` stay exactly as they are (a tool, a page with two holders in two namespaces still answers the first — phase 1 / children R and G, declared out of scope). The diff only removes configurations from the accept set; the ablation record and the CONTROLs (two namespaces, two types, same package, `sys`, no namespace, environment catalog, a view/flow/permission set) pin what stays accepted.

**Red line 2 — ambiguity is reported, never guessed.** Holds. `namespaceNameConflicts` collects every other holder per `(type, name)` (`existingPackageIds`, never empty), the message lists every conflict and every holder, the structured `conflicts[]` rides both the thrown error and the CLI row; the CLI walk reports every refused body and keeps a refused body as a holder for the bodies after it (pinned: the three-holder walk). The test "names EVERY other holder of the namespace, once per (type, name)" pins the multi-holder case.

**Red line 3 — independently releasable, readings (a)–(d).** (a) phase-1 one-holder tests untouched and reported green; `bare-name-one-holder.ts` is not in the diff. (b) bare-name behaviour unchanged for one-holder names: the CONTROL on the real load path reads both co-owners' pages back by bare name. (c) no migration, nothing stored changes shape, the rule keeps no state (reads the package records at install time). (d) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on body and changeset, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `adr-0087: not-required`. Holds.

**Per file.**

- `packages/objectql/src/namespace-co-owner-names.ts` — holds against the engine seams it cites (① 2). `namespaceNameConflicts` dedupes holders per key and conflicts per incoming `(type, name)`; `isNamespaceJudged` equals the namespace gate's exemption; `artifactPackageId` is the one id derivation (`id || name`, so a package installed under its `name` is excluded from its own sitting set correctly). The `\u0000` key separator cannot collide with a `name` (SnakeCase grammars). Message and line are the one spelling both doors use.
- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` — `refuseNamespaceNameConflicts` reads `this.metadata.get('package')` records' `manifest.namespace` and projects each through `namespacePackageOf`; placed as ① 5. `NamespaceNameConflictError` carries `code`, `status`, `httpStatus` 422 like `NamespaceConflictError` and `BareNameConflictError` on `main`, so the REST passthrough (`status`) and the CLI envelope (`httpStatus`) both read it — the envelope is consistent with the namespace gate. Composition with phase 1's `tool`: this rule runs before `refuseBareNameConflicts`, carries the same code and status, and the test pins that after `sealBareNameHolders()` a same-namespace tool is refused by THIS class; a cross-namespace tool stays the bare-name rule's (after #31661) — the two never disagree about a refusal, only about the door's timing, as the module doc says. #31661's hunks (`registerItem` comment, `bare-name-one-holder.ts`) are not touched.
- `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` — exports exactly what the CLI consumes; the class stays private as its siblings do.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts` — the walk is `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, the order `AppPlugin` → `manifest.register` → `registerApp(body)` installs in (ADR-0130 D4/D5), each body against the bodies before it; a stack without `packages[]` returns `[]` (one package, nothing to hold beside). Same predicate, same sentence, no second copy. Stated bounds (installed packages of the deployment invisible; residual unjudged) are true.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` (2c-bis) and `compile.ts` (3a-ter) — the call sits right after the parse, beside 2c/3a, with 2c/3a's faces (`--json` `errors` rows carrying `warningsSoFar()` and `conversionNotices`; text `printError` + `printBulletList` with `JSON_FULL_LIST_REMEDY`), exit 1 before any artifact write. The parity roster row classifies it where both commands call it.
- Tests — the twelve-type `describe.each` at both doors, the real-load-path refusal per family, the spawn test asserting message equality across doors, the ablations in the PR body (17/56, 1/4, 14/29 red) show each door's call is load-bearing. The two forced rows are correctly keyed (① 8).

**Findings.**

- **S1 (should-fix) — an undeclared accept-set change at `os validate` / `os build`, through the walk's resolver.** `findNamespaceNameRefusals` is the first call either command makes to `@objectstack/core`'s `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` (the sibling walks — `view-container-names.ts`, `picklist-references`, `override-declarations`, `collect-docs` — read `artifactPackages`, a plain map, and `collect-docs.ts` states "this collector has no duplicate-id refusal of its own"). The resolver throws `DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE` (422) for an artifact declaring one package id twice and `resolvePluginOrder`'s bare `[Kernel] Circular dependency detected` (no code) for a dependency cycle inside the artifact. The stack schema at step 2 parses `packages: z.array(ArtifactPackageSchema)`, so a malformed entry is already refused there, but neither of those two was refused by `os validate` on base: they now exit 1 through the commands' catch-all (`error` + `errorCodeFields` in `--json`, a printed line in text), not as an `errors` row, and the cycle carries no code. Nothing is loosened and both artifacts never booted — `stack-collections.ts` records the house position that a named 422 beats that silence — so this is not a narrowing beyond the twelve types and not a maintainer question. But the Clause-② sentence ("Nothing is widened"; two refusals named) does not name it, and the cycle refusal reaches the author without an envelope. Fix: name the two pass-through refusals in the PR body's Clause-② sentence (a body edit, no new head) and, when the branch next moves, in the changeset; optionally catch the resolver's refusal in the walk and emit it as a row with its code. Not a must-fix.
- **N1 (nit) — sitting holders are read from the projected record, the incoming from the live manifest.** `toRecordManifest` drops class instances, so a `plugins[]` entry that is a plugin instance carrying a covered collection counts on the incoming side and is absent on the sitting side — an order-dependent gap for a shape `GET /packages` cannot serve either. State the bound in the module doc beside the residual bound, or run `namespacePackageOf` over `toRecordManifest(manifest)` on the incoming side too.
- **N2 (nit) — hot re-registration order.** On a running registry, moving a covered name from co-owner A to co-owner B in one upgraded artifact is refused when B re-registers before A (A's stale record still holds the name); the cold boot starts from an empty registry so it is unaffected, and `refuseCoOwnedObjectNameCollision` has the identical disposition for an object (it reads the sitting owner), so this is inherited from the ruled sibling. `os validate` walks only the new bodies and accepts that artifact, so the two doors can disagree on this one hot path. State it as a bound.
- **N3 (nit) — the residual.** Top-level items of a `packages[]` stack that no body declares are registered under the stack's own id without an install (`MetadataPlugin.registerUnclaimedTopLevel`) and are judged at neither door, as the PR body and module say; the stack manifest can carry the same namespace as its packages. Already in the acceptance notes; it should become a filed follow-up card (Prime Directive 10: a known gap in enforcement is filed, not only noted).
- **N4 (nit) — names.** `NamespaceNameConflictError` vs the existing `NamespaceConflictError`; module `namespace-co-owner-names.ts` vs exports `namespaceName*`; no `rename` suggestion carried as `BareNameConflict.rename` is (the sentence says rename generically). No change required.
- **N5 (nit) — `itemName` requires a non-empty string** where `resolveMetadataItemName` takes any truthy `name`/`id`. Unreachable for a spec-valid item (names are strings); no change required.

No must-fix. S1 is a declaration gap on an accept-set change that is the boot's own; the seat decides whether to take it as a body edit on this head or with the next push.
